verdict.summary: The opt-in DualLeafV1 host commitment builder is correct and complete for its explicitly limited host-only scope. It reuses the established RDFC10 canonicalization and canonical triple order, preserves the flat graph sponge and salt-scoped blank-node encoding, routes the three declared hookable datatypes through their existing same-leaf encoders, and fails the whole commitment on rejected hookable lexicals or uncommittable RDF 1.2 terms. The load-bearing fail-closed test exercises the real commit_triples_dual path and distinguishes the forbidden downgrade from a valid canonical sibling; the ordering test compares against the existing commitment pipeline and independently recomputes leaves and the sponge. Public documentation accurately describes the parallel-builder scope, unrouted datatype seams, absent circuit/verifier integration, INV-VL downgrade, research-grade status, and pending external audit. No uncaveated soundness/privacy claim or security regression was found.
